publisher: U.S. Department of the Treasury, Bureau of the Fiscal Service
title_or_table: Monthly Statement of the Public Debt, Table II, Statutory Debt Limit
table_id: MSPD Table 2 (Fiscal Data mspd_table_2), lines Total Public Debt Subject to Limit, Statutory Debt Limit, Balance of Statutory Debt Limit
universe_or_base: Federal debt counted against the limit set in law (31 U.S.C. 3101), held by the public and by government accounts
unit: millions of dollars, nominal, exactly as published; a chart rounds once, at print
vintage: Monthly Statements of the Public Debt as served on November 11, 2026
qualification: An empty limit cell is a month when the table shows the limit as zero, which the studio reads as a suspension of the limit (it was suspended until January 1, 2025, by the Fiscal Responsibility Act of 2023, a reading not checked on govinfo.gov today); the limit of $41,104 billion is the one in force at the latest month, after Public Law 119-21 (July 4, 2025) raised it by $5 trillion. The studio did not read the statute today, so a chart that cites the law checks it on govinfo.gov first

debt_subject_to_limit_millions.description: total public debt subject to limit, as published

room_under_limit_millions.description: balance of the statutory limit, as published

printed_source_line: Source: U.S. Department of the Treasury, Monthly Statement of the Public Debt, Table II, statutory debt limit, October 31, 2026, United States. Retrieved November 11, 2026. Debt subject to the limit, held by the public and by government accounts.
